Outrage flares over California's new small business directory.
Evidence: Optional demographic filters, No male/white label, Online backlash
#Aletheia #California

Critics claim California's new 'Made in California' shopping site discriminates against white and male business owners by omitting specific identity filters.
Stated Judgement: (+1.00, +0.00) — Lesser Good

The directory aids consumer discovery for minority or women-owned brands based on in-state production. All businesses qualify regardless of demographic labels.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.05, -0.10) — Greater Evil

Verdict: CONDITIONAL — Awakening into Destruction.
A routine economic promotional directory is weaponized into a culture-war grievance to manufacture partisan outrage.

Integrity: Partially Distorted (Hypocrisy: 3.40, z: 2)

Sub-Audits Breakdown:
- NY Post Coverage: COND (-0.60, -0.70) — Amplifies partisan outrage over administrative omissions.
- State Initiative: PASS (0.50, 0.50) — Promotes local CA small businesses neutrally.
California launched a 'Made in California' portal managed by the Small Business Advocate to help buyers find local goods. Optional search tags highlight diverse business groups.

The Poison:
Transforming a standard economic directory into an ideological battleground, distracting from genuine small business support.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing a consumer marketing tool with a restrictive government mandate. The error treats optional demographic tags as mandatory exclusions.

Social Physics Analysis:
Critics run a Smart Selfish Maneuver by framing a standard commercial directory as anti-white discrimination, manufacturing grievance to score political points.

The Trajectory: The Path of Awakening into Destruction.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Lesser Evil. Misrepresenting promotional tags as systemic exclusion builds toxic polarization.

The Unavoidable Truth: Optional consumer search tags do not bar any qualified California business from participating in the state directory.

The Unavoidable Lie: The promotional site intentionally excludes white men to enforce systematic discrimination.

Alethekanon:
Culture-war commentators weaponized an optional business directory filter to manufacture tribal outrage where none existed.

Awwthekanon:
It is sad to see genuine efforts to support local artisans get twisted into bitter arguments about identity instead of celebrating homegrown California work.

Brothekanon:
They turned a simple shop-local website into another internet flame war over who gets a search tag.

Spirithekanon:
"Dwell on what is right, what is pure, what is lovely, whatever has good report." Philippians 4:8 FAIL
Amplifying manufactured outrage over routine directory tags fractures community trust for fleeting political points.

Stated Claim / Post Context:
Outrage as state’s ‘Made in California’ site hawking homegrown products excludes white men from identity filters

A new “Made in California” website selling locally made products allows buyers to search for goods from brands operated by women, minorities and a host of other groups.

Actual Article Body:
Switch between CA and NY editions here.

See more of our coverage in your search results.

A new “Made in California” website selling locally made products is catching flak for allowing would-be buyers to search for goods from brands operated by women, minorities and a host of other groups — but not male- or white-owned businesses.

Conservative activist Christopher Rufo and other critics called attention to the website’s optional demographic filters, which include Black-owned, Native American-owned, LGBTQ-owned and Veteran-Owned businesses, among others.

There is no designation for businesses owned by male or white Californians.

The biggest news, opinion and culture shaping California right now.

Please provide a valid email.

By clicking above you agree to the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy.

Never miss a story

The omission prompted a wave of online anger, with one X user declaring: “White men if you are not a veteran you are useless.”

Another called for legal action, writing, “They need to be sued for discrimination by erasure then.”

A third lamented: “Sigh. A nice idea poisoned by identity politics.”

Yet another weighed in: “I miss my state but don’t miss the BS. The California dream on display.”

The missing label does not mean those business owners are barred from participating.

Gov. Gavin Newsom announced the initiative on Aug. 28. Managed by the California Office of the Small Business Advocate, the program is designed to help consumers and corporate buyers find products manufactured in the Golden State.

To qualify, a product must have at least 51% of its wholesale value added within the state. Certified businesses can appear in the official public directory and use the “Made in California” seal on their packaging and marketing materials.
